Verdicts given on a served map

Source: R/notes.R
rr_verdicts.Rd

A map served with rr_serve(verdicts = ) takes the reader's verdict on the features of a layer whose popup has a verdict (rr_layer()): its questions in a feature's popup, a button for each answer, a box for the name an answer points at (other, with the names in view offered), and the feature's note where the verdict asks for one. Each answer is a row added to a .csv file, never a row changed: when, the layer, the feature (its value of the verdict's field), the question, the answer, the other feature's name, the note, the feature's title, its place (the feature's own for a point, else where it was clicked) and the zoom. The note is a question of its own, "note", its text the answer. A later answer to a question replaces the earlier, and an empty one withdraws it. The page draws a mark on each feature judged: the first question's answer its fill, the second's its ring. A review written down where it is made, and read back as data: what a map shows can be checked by hand, and the checks counted. A file of 2026.11.09, before the questions, reads as the question "verdict" with no other names.

Usage

rr_verdicts(path, all = FALSE)

Arguments

path

The verdicts' file (.csv).

all

FALSE, each feature's current answer to each question (the last, none where it was withdrawn; a note where it has a text); TRUE, every answer given, in the order given.

Value

A data frame: time (UTC, as text), layer, id, question, value, other, text, title, lon, lat, zoom; no rows when there is no file.

Examples

# a map whose harbours take a verdict each:
# popup = list(click = "harbours-fill", title = "SI_HARB",
#              verdict = list(field = "SI_HARB", text = TRUE,
#                             options = list(list(value = "right", label = "right"),
#                                            list(value = "wrong", label = "wrong"))))
# rr_serve(m, verdicts = "harbour_verdicts.csv")
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
rr_verdicts(f) # none yet
#>  [1] time     layer    id       question value    other    text     title   
#>  [9] lon      lat      zoom    
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
